t.1.21.1: When Vasiṣṭha had spoken thus, King Daśaratha, his face beaming with joy, summoned his son Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.1.21.3: King Daśaratha, having kissed his beloved son on the head, gave him to the son of Kuśika with a deeply gladdened inner self.
t.1.21.2: Him, for whom the rites of blessing had been performed by his mother and by his father Daśaratha, and who had been consecrated with auspicious mantras by the family priest Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.21.4: Then, seeing lotus-eyed Rāma gone with Viśvāmitra, a dustless wind, pleasant to the touch, blew at that time.
t.1.21.5: When the great-souled one set out, there was a great shower of flowers, the sound of the gods' drums, and the resounding blare of conches and kettledrums.
t.1.21.6: Viśvāmitra went in front; after him came the greatly renowned Rāma, wearing side-locks of hair like a crow's wings and bearing a bow, and Saumitri followed him.
t.1.21.7: Wearing quivers, bows in hand, lighting up the ten directions like a pair of three-headed serpents, the two noble youths followed the great-souled Viśvāmitra, as the two Aśvins follow Pitāmaha.
t.1.21.8: With finger-guards of iguana leather bound on and bearing swords, the two greatly radiant ones followed him, like the two youthful sons of Pāvaka following the inconceivable god Sthāṇu.
t.1.21.9: Having gone a yojana and a half, on the southern bank of the Sarayū, Viśvāmitra addressed him in a sweet voice, saying, “Rāma!”
t.1.21.10: Take water, dear child, and let no time be lost. Receive the collection of mantras, Balā and likewise Atibalā.
t.1.21.11: There will be no fatigue for you, nor fever, nor any change of your form; nor will the Nairṛtas overpower you while you are asleep or off your guard.
t.1.21.12: There is no one on earth equal to you in the strength of your two arms, O Rāma, nor in the three worlds could there be anyone equal to you.
t.1.21.14: When this pair of sciences has been obtained, there will be none equal to you. Balā and Atibalā are the two mothers of all knowledge.
t.1.21.13: In good fortune, in courtesy, in knowledge and in firmness of judgment, no one superior to you is to be found, nor anyone your equal in the world, O sinless one.
t.1.21.15: O Rāma, best of men, hunger and thirst will not befall you as you recite Balā and Atibalā on the road, O Rāghava; and as you study them, this twofold knowledge and matchless fame on earth will also be yours.
t.1.21.16: These two lores, daughters of the Grandsire and endowed with splendour, are to be bestowed upon you, O Kākutstha, for you are worthy of them, O righteous one.
t.1.21.18: Then Rāma, pure and with a joyful face, touched water and received those two sciences from the great sage of purified soul. Endowed with that knowledge, Rāma of great valour shone forth.
t.1.21.17: Truly, all these many virtues are already in you; of this there is no doubt. Yet these two, nourished by austerity, will take on many forms.
t.1.21.19: Having rendered all the services due to a teacher to the son of Kuśika, the three spent that night there on the bank of the Sarayū in great comfort.
